data.name: Guide.IntroBody
data.value: Ceasy observes Codex Desktop tasks locally and brings interruptions that need attention into one workspace.

data.name: Guide.MonitoringBody
data.value: Monitoring begins when Ceasy opens. It only reads task state and does not rewrite the Codex installation, state databases, or conversation records.

data.name: Guide.DefaultBody
data.value: New settings start in monitor-only mode with automatic recovery off. Upgrading older settings also turns automatic recovery off. Until you enable it, Ceasy reports failures without automatically continuing failed turns.

data.name: Guide.AuthorizationBody
data.value: The title-bar Automatic recovery switch controls recovery permission; per-conversation protection controls task scope. Preset messages are authorized separately. Turning automatic recovery off does not pause an authorized preset queue.

data.name: Guide.NavigationConversations
data.value: Conversations: search and filter tasks, then inspect current state, the latest reply, and recovery history. The message entry opens presets for that conversation.

data.name: Guide.NavigationActivity
data.value: Activity: review recent monitoring events and workflow execution records.

data.name: Guide.NavigationGuardrails
data.value: Guardrails: check recovery permission and configure attempt budgets, counting, and follow-up backoff. Changing these values does not remove a safety lock.

data.name: Guide.NavigationKeepAlive
data.value: Keep-alive: choose held conversations or a sentinel destination, configure the interval and message, and review actual sends.

data.name: Guide.NavigationPreferences
data.value: Preferences: adjust language, appearance, startup, update checks, and task discovery; open the local data folder or this guide.

data.name: Guide.PresetBody
data.value: Open presets from the target conversation, add content, and choose after normal completion or a local scheduled time. Drag the left grip to reorder. Edits and ordering remain drafts until you save.

data.name: Guide.PresetAuthorization
data.value: Sending requires explicit permission from the corresponding queue, message, or workflow rule, plus conversation-protection, target, Desktop channel, composer-state, and duplicate-prevention checks. Pause the corresponding queue or rule to stop it. An uncertain send is not automatically repeated.

data.name: Guide.RecoveryEligible
data.value: Enabling recovery still requires a verified latest failed turn and an available Desktop channel. A task interrupted after useful output may qualify to continue; a failure with no output does not by itself allow a resend.

data.name: Guide.RecoveryBlocked
data.value: User stops, 401/403, authentication failures, exhausted credit, content policy, and context limits never trigger automatic recovery. An error code without complete terminal-state evidence does not authorize a send.

data.name: Guide.RecoveryEvidence
data.value: For a safety lock, missing evidence, or an uncertain result, inspect the conversation state and activity first. Ceasy does not append duplicate messages to bypass resend limits or modify Codex to support an unknown version.

data.name: Guide.KeepAliveBody
data.value: Keep-alive sends configured messages to explicitly selected held conversations. Sentinel mode uses a chosen destination after any conversation receives a reply. It does not guarantee server capacity, queue priority, or a continuous connection.

data.name: Guide.KeepAliveAuthorization
data.value: Choose conversations and review the interval and message on the Keep-alive page before explicitly enabling its master switch. Monitor-only mode blocks keep-alive sends. Sending remains guarded; runtime state and send records show the actual result.

data.name: Guide.TrayBody
data.value: With Close to tray enabled, closing the window keeps monitoring and authorized behavior running in the background. Click the Ceasy notification-area icon to reopen it. Right-click the icon and choose Exit to stop the application.
